lead: Exploring the intersection of technology and health, from AI-driven tools to innovative wearables.

stories.title: ChatGPT Health Is Rolling Out to Everyone, but I Don’t Trust It
stories.summary: As ChatGPT Health becomes available to a wider audience, concerns about privacy and data protection have surfaced. Critics argue that the privacy safeguards have deteriorated since the feature's initial announcement, raising questions about the reliability and safety of using AI for health-related inquiries. The rollout prompts a deeper discussion on the ethical implications of AI in healthcare.

stories.title: How to Take Creatine for the (Possible) Mental Health Benefits
stories.summary: The potential mental health benefits of creatine supplementation are being explored, with mixed but promising evidence. While traditionally associated with physical performance, creatine is now being scrutinized for its effects on cognitive function and mood. This article discusses how to properly take creatine to possibly enhance mental well-being.

stories.title: Oura Ring 5 review: a stunning generational leap for smart rings
stories.summary: The new Oura Ring 5 represents a significant upgrade in health-tracking wearables, featuring a slimmer design and enhanced functionality. With improved battery life and comfort, it aims to integrate seamlessly into daily life. However, users must subscribe for full access to its features, raising questions about the cost of advanced health technology.

stories.title: Why Bevel Is a Way Better App for the Fitbit Air Than Google Health
stories.summary: The Bevel app is highlighted as a superior alternative for Fitbit Air users compared to Google Health. With its user-friendly interface and better metric tracking capabilities, Bevel provides a more streamlined experience without intrusive AI features. This comparison emphasizes the importance of app choice in effectively managing health data.

stories.title: Atos launches sovereign cloud service to power comeback
stories.summary: Atos has introduced a sovereign cloud platform aimed at European public sector entities, including healthcare providers. This initiative is part of a broader effort to enhance data control and compliance with European regulations. The move reflects a growing trend towards digital sovereignty in healthcare and other sectors.

stories.title: Sovereign AI has become the public-sector CIO’s control problem
stories.summary: The integration of AI in public services raises significant control issues for CIOs, particularly regarding data management and operational sovereignty. This article discusses the complexities of maintaining authority over AI systems, emphasizing the need for robust governance frameworks to ensure accountability in public health applications.

stories.title: The new value architecture of the AI-native SaaS era
stories.summary: The shift towards AI-native SaaS is transforming how companies measure success and value. Traditional metrics are being replaced by new frameworks that focus on credits and outcomes, impacting pricing and operational strategies. This evolution has significant implications for health tech companies leveraging AI to enhance service delivery.

stories.title: Getting a grip on shadow tokens and AI blowouts
stories.summary: The article explores the risks associated with unregulated AI token consumption in organizations, particularly in healthcare settings. It highlights the need for better governance and financial oversight to prevent budget overruns and ensure sustainable AI deployment. This is crucial as healthcare increasingly adopts AI technologies.
